ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.27 (voucher per NS-7) for the non-exempt off-route segment; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip; metered fare rises with distance, so the one off-route segment [F3] must be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1]. The record shows no incident on the replaced stretch, so RD-4 gives no exemption; the only route-related speed band (Kampong Bahru Rd, band 2, 18:16–18:34) sits on the optimal route and under RD-4(b) is corroborative only and not a standalone exemption [F11][F14][RD-4].

The decisive element is RD-5 timing: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment began [RD-5]. The only chat message is the driver's 18:30 question, "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" [F8]; the rider never answered it — the chat record is complete and holds a single, timestamped message [F9]. The segment ran 18:34–18:45 [F3], so no rider agreement preceded it. The driver's post-trip assertion that the rider raised "no objection" is a claim that appears only in his statement, which under G11 is not consent [F10][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts [RD-5]. RD-3 does not help either side: the rider named no place and no stop was measured in the segment, and RD-3 governs rider-requested stops, not driver-proposed route changes [F8][RD-3].

Amount: only the extra km of the non-exempt segment are refundable, at this trip's per-km rate [RD-2]. Rate = $18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.4098/km [F7]; 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.2736 → $6.27 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The segment's extra distance (4.45 km) is the trace's measure of that segment, and the trace's formula is Σ extra_km × $1.4098/km, so the figure is taken from the segment's own extra km rather than from the trip-total excess [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, and profile facts never decide the case on their own [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The driver's 18:30 message proposes going "round via Zion Road" and the record contains no rider reply before the segment started at 18:34; the complete, timestamped chat [F9] shows no rider agreement, and the driver's post-trip statement that the rider did not object is his own claim, not consent (G11). Under RD-5 a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts; RD-3(a) is unavailable because the rider named no place and no stop was measured in this segment.
